en.title: Maximum Passengers on a Round Trip Through a Grid
en.description:
Go from the top-left to the bottom-right moving only right/down, then return moving only left/up. −1 is a wall, 0 is an empty cell, and 1 is one passenger; once a cell is passed, its passenger is picked up and not counted again. If there is no valid outbound path, return 0. Find the maximum total number of passengers.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n lines of the matrix. 1≤n≤100, and each cell is −1, 0, or 1. The start and end cells may also hold a passenger or a wall; if either is a wall, there is no valid trip.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 1; 5; 1. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Reverse the return trip so that it becomes two people walking simultaneously from the top-left to the bottom-right. The shared step count t determines column = t−row, so the DP state only records the two rows; a shared cell adds its passenger only once.
